# browserjs_policy_document (Data Source)

Builds a policy in the JSON format from HCL, for the `json` argument of `browserjs_session_policy`. It calls nothing; it only renders JSON.

A policy denies by default. An operation is allowed if it is not in `deny_operations` and is either in `allow_operations` or satisfies one of the `rule` blocks. A `browser_execute` call is allowed only if every operation in it is.

The operations are `click`, `evaluate`, `navigate`, `press`, `screenshot`, `select`, `setContent`, `setViewport`, `type`, `url` and `wait`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Fill in forms on two sites: printable text only, a few keys, sane viewport
# sizes, no script.
data "browserjs_policy_document" "form_filling" {
  description      = "Fill in forms on two sites."
  allow_operations = ["click", "select", "wait", "screenshot", "url"]
  deny_operations  = ["evaluate", "setContent"]

  rule {
    operation = "navigate"
    constraint {
      parameter = "url"
      hosts     = ["forms.example.org", "*.intranet.example.org"]
    }
  }

  rule {
    operation = "type"
    constraint {
      parameter  = "text"
      max_length = 200
      pattern    = "^[\\x20-\\x7E]*$"
    }
  }

  rule {
    operation = "press"
    constraint {
      parameter = "key"
      allowed   = ["Enter", "Tab", "Escape"]
    }
  }

  rule {
    operation = "setViewport"
    constraint {
      parameter = "width"
      min       = 320
      max       = 1920
    }
    constraint {
      parameter = "height"
      min       = 200
      max       = 1200
    }
  }
}

resource "browserjs_session_policy" "forms" {
  session_id  = browserjs_session.forms.id
  managed_url = "https://github.com/example/infra/tree/main/browserjs"
  json        = data.browserjs_policy_document.form_filling.json
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `allow_operations` (Set of String) Operations allowed with any parameters. `"*"` means every operation.
- `deny_operations` (Set of String) Operations refused whatever is allowed.
- `description` (String) What the policy is for; shown in the UI.
- `rule` (Block List) An operation allowed when every one of its constraints passes. A rule with no constraint allows the operation as `allow_operations` does. At most 64. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `json` (String) The rendered policy, keys in a stable order.

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `operation` (String) The operation the rule allows.

Optional:

- `constraint` (Block List) A condition on one parameter of the operation. A constrained parameter that is absent from the call fails. At least one condition is required. At most 16 per rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule--constraint))

<a id="nestedblock--rule--constraint"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.constraint`

Required:

- `parameter` (String) The name of the parameter, such as `url` for `navigate` or `text` for `type`.

Optional:

- `allowed` (List of String) The parameter is one of these strings.
- `allowed_booleans` (List of Boolean) The parameter is one of these booleans. Rendered into the same `allowed` list as `allowed` and `allowed_numbers`.
- `allowed_numbers` (List of Number) The parameter is one of these numbers. Rendered into the same `allowed` list as `allowed` and `allowed_booleans`.
- `hosts` (Set of String) The parameter is a URL whose host is one of these: an exact name, or `*.name` for any subdomain of `name` (not `name` itself).
- `max` (Number) The parameter is a number, at most this.
- `max_length` (Number) The parameter is a string of at most this many characters.
- `min` (Number) The parameter is a number, at least this.
- `pattern` (String) The parameter is a string matching this regular expression (RE2 syntax, unanchored unless it anchors itself).
- `schemes` (Set of String) The parameter is a URL with one of these schemes (`http`, `https`). With `hosts` and without this, both are accepted.
